newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY AUTO FIRM RABA COULD SEE BOURSE FLOTATION.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY AUTO FIRM RABA COULD SEE BOURSE FLOTATION.

text.p: Hungary's state privatisation agency (APV) said on Thursday the privatisation of auto company Raba Rt should be completed in 1997 through a combination of a private tender and a public offer.
APV also said that while it will be looking to attract strategic investors, it will limit the stake of any single buyer to 20 percent at most.

"APV would like to see at least some shares floated on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE)," an APV source told Reuters. "It also wants a strategic investors but each investor will be limited to 15 or 20 percent."
"APV want to offer 15 percent but the employees want 20," she added.

The official said that APV planned to acquire from the state-owned Hungarian Investment and Development Bank (MBFB) the 49.6 percent stake the bank currently holds in Raba through an equity swap and add this to APV's current 32.3 percent stake.
"APV will offer to MBFB shares in other companies in return," she said.
"This will give APV 81.9 percent and after three percent is given over to local authorities, 10 to 15 percent will go to employees and the rest will be available to investors."

The source added that some of the remaining 60-plus percent will be offered in a private tender to strategic investors and the rest will be publicly offered to domestic small investors, followed by a listing on the BSE.
She said that Raba needs three to 3.6 billion forints of investment and this will be a condition of any tender.
Raba Rt said earlier this month it expected its fifth consecutive year of profits in 1996 on the strength of an accelerating globalisation drive.

"In 1996, Raba will achieve over 27 billion forints in turnover and one billion forints in pre-tax profits," Barnabas Zalan, Raba's general manager, said at an event celebrating the company's 100th year of operation in Gyor in western Hungary.

The company, whose full name is Raba Magyar Vagon -es Gepgyar Rt>, posted a pre-tax profit of 700 million forints on 23.7 billion forints in revenue in 1995 and a pre-tax profit of 547 million forints on 20.3 billion forints in revenue in 1994.

Raba, a supplier of major parts for the bus and truck industy, already claims to be Hungary's top exporter to the United States. Recently it started sales to Japan and Korea, while projects in China and Russia are underway.
